title: 8.4 Volume of a Solid: Slicing

icans: I can write the area of a cross section that is a square, semicircle, or triangle.
I can find the side of a cross section from the base region.
I can find a volume by slicing.

vocab: the __________ you see when a solid is cut by a plane
V = ∫ A(x) dx, where A(x) is the area of the cross __________ at x

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Squares: A = s², where s is the _______________ of the base at x.

blocks.stem: The base is the region under y = √x from 0 to 4. Cross sections ⊥ the x-axis are squares. Find V.
Same base, but the cross sections are semicircles. Find V.
The base is the region between y = 1 − x² and the x-axis. Cross sections are equilateral triangles. Find V.
Write A(x) for isosceles right triangles with a leg on the base.
The base is the triangle under y = 2 − x in the first quadrant. Cross sections are squares. Find V.

(AP® Practice) The base is the region between y = x and y = x². Cross sections ⊥ the x-axis are squares. The volume is
(A) 1/30   (B) 1/6   (C) 2/15   (D) π/30

tickets.stem: A cross section is a semicircle with diameter s. Write A.
The base is under y = √x from 0 to 2; squares. Find V.
